Quiet shift. If anything with teeth shows up, you'll hear me laughing before you hear the bell.

Zevara smiled this week. Actual smile. The warren's sealed and the city's still standing. I'm taking full credit and handing you most of it.
Next time something ugly crawls out of the ground, I'm not even worried. That's new for me. Don't make it weird.

entities.locked_toast: Sodden timber and tarred rope, jammed wall to wall. You could haul at it for an hour, or you could burn it, if you had the means to make fire.

entities.toast: Phosphor moss clings to the brick, glowing a sick, cold green. Cool to the touch, and it hisses faintly when your shadow crosses it.

entities.toast: An old Drake drainage marker, its glyphs half-swallowed by grime. You can just make out a map of channels — and a fresh scratch, shaped like a spider, gouged over the third cistern.

entities.toast: A ruined crate, half-sunk in silt. Merchant stamps still show under the rot: lost cargo, swallowed by the sewers and picked clean.

entities.observe: Cable-thick silk, black-and-silver banded, stretched wall to wall. Not a house spider's work. Something with a shield on its back spun this, and recently.
entities.toast: Ropes of banded silk choke the side passage, strong as wire. Wrapped in it, drained pale: a rat, a boot, something that used to be a Watchman's lantern.

entities.observe: A ring of fire-blackened stones, the ash inside long dead and cold. Something sat here in the dark and knew how to keep a fire — or learned how, the way they say these things learn, when the moon is full and their minds come clear.
entities.toast: A fire-pit ringed with blackened stones, its ashes cold. Whoever tended it had hands enough to strike a spark, and left gnawed bones banked around the edge, cracked for their marrow.

entities.observe: A midden of cracked bones, marrow sucked clean. Gnoll, most of them. A few too large to name. They have been sorted, almost stacked, as though something down here counts its meals and keeps the score.
entities.toast: A heap of gnawed bones, splintered for their marrow. Some are Gnoll. One is a Drake's. They are stacked, not scattered. And that is worse than if they had been.

entities._comment: The deep_tunnels route-fight -- a Raskghar scout PAIR barring the way to the warren. Interact-only (no trigger_radius) so QA/A3 control the start; deep_descent clears it via combat_autoplay. Fought in cave_mouth (the generic cave arena); the deep_warren arena is reserved for A3's boss. on_victory banks cleared_raskghar_scouts.
entities.observe: Two of them crouch where the tunnel narrows, moon-grey and mountain-shouldered, knuckles to the stone. Their small eyes track you without blinking. Between you and the deeper dark, they are the door — and the lock.

entities._comment: The widened-gallery marker -- the 'warren door' deep_descent reaches (its terminal beat). A flavor threshold prop in A2; A3 wired the Awakened Raskghar boss encounter (deep_warren arena) here / just beyond it, plus the Relc party/veto beat. 8d C1 (issue #14) B3 wiring: `door_when` gated on `horns_delve_started` -- the SAME counter/mirror-cell as dungeon_approach's `gallery_seal_anchor`, this entity's own reopened-gallery pair. Structurally safe: `horns_delve_started` requires `post_game` to even be offered (Olesm's stipend option), and `post_game` implies the full Act III backbone including `cleared_the_warren`/`raskghar_sealed` (test_fixture_coherence.gd's own POST_GAME_BACKBONE) -- so this door_when can never intercept a FIRST-time arrival here; the one-time `reached_the_warren` flavor beat below (deep_descent's own canonical) always already fired before the gate could ever be met.
entities.observe: The passage opens into a vast pillared gallery, its floor packed smooth by generations of pacing feet. Eyes catch your light far back in the dark and slide away. This is where they den, and where the big one waits, breathing slow in the black.

variants.toast: The gallery is silent now. The pacing tracks are old and dust-softened; nothing breathes in the dark ahead. Past the emptied den, the stone the Watch sealed stands unbroken.

visual_states.observe: Claw-gouges score the pillars, going quiet toward the back. The den is empty — cleared, then sealed. Whatever the warren was, it is a grave and a door now.

entities.toast: The tunnel widens into a pillared gallery, the air stirring with breath that is not your own. Something large shifts in the dark ahead, and the pacing scuffs go quiet. You have found the warren.

door_when.open_toast: The gallery floor slopes down past where the den used to be, into a chamber someone else has clearly been surveying.

entities._comment: THE BOSS encounter -- the Awakened Raskghar + 2 scout adds, fought in the deep_warren arena. Interact-triggered (no trigger_radius, so QA/the player choose to engage; it sits just past the warren_mouth threshold at (12,7), reachable by standing at (12,6) facing down). Carries a `conversation` (relc_descent = the Relc join/veto beat, the interact.encounter branch runs it before combat): the [Go together.] branch banks `relc_joined_descent`, satisfying THIS entity's `ally_requires` so Relc fields as an ally; the [I go alone.] branch banks `went_alone` and NEVER banks relc_joined_descent, so the roster fields no ally (the honest, measured 0.04 solo cell -- the player chose it). Both branches end on a `start_combat: awakened_boss` effect (self-reference). on_victory banks `cleared_the_warren`; the seal-beat resolutions (Zevara/Olesm) consume that and bank the Act III advance key `raskghar_sealed` after the player returns to the surface (NOT here -- victory != sealed, per the acts data trace). respawns:false + no persistent flag => the boss is removed for good on victory (no re-fight). Balance: sim_combat_batch.gd BOSS_CELLS (gated 0.6-0.75 vs warrior2+Relc, measured solo).
entities.observe: It fills the gallery mouth like a landslide that learned to breathe: upright, moon-grey, a pale mane over shoulders wider than a doorway. Old scars cross its hide, and a Gnoll's picked bones lie stacked at its feet. Its eyes hold on you with something worse than hunger: thought.

guild._comment: The Adventurer's Guild interior (16x12), reached via guild_door on the street (28,3; now a real door, not a toast). entities.observe: A Drake behind a counter she clearly wishes were taller. Tired, sharp, quick with a ledger. She has sized up a hundred adventurers today and found most of them wanting.
entities.friendly_line: ...Huh. You're actually pleasant. That's rare on this side of the counter. Fine - your paperwork jumps the line today. Don't make it weird.
talk_pool: Guild's the usual mess. Bounties on the board, arguments over the board, somebody bleeding near the board.
Need something stamped, filed, or explained slowly? That is the job. Mostly the slow part.
Try not to die out there. It is a mountain of paperwork when you do, and guess who is the mountain.
New face. You'll fit right in - everyone here is chasing coin they have not earned yet.
entities._comment_stages: Lifted verbatim from docs/design/social-2-staging/selys_stages.json (staging_note annotation stripped). Two stages only. lines: Oh good, a face that doesn't come with a complaint form. You can stand there as long as you like.
Tell Erin her letters are still too long. And that I read all of them. Do not pass on the second part.
Rough week on the board. If you're taking work, take the sane jobs. I flag the sane ones. It's not a service everyone gets.

dialogue.speaker: Selys
dialogue.text: Adventurers. Always tracking mud in.

entities.second_visit_toast: The Request Board. Your slip is still logged at the desk. The board does not care how it's going.
entities.observe: Rates set by the Guild. Complaints to the Guildmistress in person. Bring patience. — S.S.

They've got witch trouble, or so the last one through here said -- crops going bad, nobody saying why out loud. No bounty on it, just word passed along. Ask the Guild about the road if you're curious.

board_rumors._comment: Locked shape 1's Guild-board letter beat, same idiom as rumor_riverfarm (a DISTINCT board_rumors entry, not a bounties.json posting -- that pool's size stays load-bearing for canonical rotation windows). board_rumors.copy: A LETTER, sealed in wax gone slightly soft from handling, addressed to no one by name. Inside: impeccable handwriting regrets to inform you of a small disagreement in Invrisil concerning a mutual acquaintance's good name, and would consider it a personal favor -- and a professional one -- if a stranger to the city might look into it. The witch at Riverfarm keeps the stones, should the distance prove an obstacle. Signed only with a small drawing of a hat. The Guildmistress's clerk says it arrived by very ordinary post, which is itself the strangest part.

board_rumors._comment: 8d C1 (issue #14) 'What the Seal Kept' seeding beat -- SIGNPOST only, same idiom as rumor_riverfarm/rumor_invrisil (browse-only, banks a flavor-only counter no gate reads). Points the reader at Olesm by name (the stipend is HIS option, in olesm_intro.json, gated separately on post_game) rather than naming a location a player could act on directly from the board itself.
board_rumors.copy: A WATCH NOTICE, freshly pinned. The reopened gallery under the old seal is to be surveyed properly before the Council calls it settled -- volunteers with Guild standing should see Olesm Swifttail at the frontage desk. Pay is Watch-scale. The notice does not say what 'properly' means, and nobody pinning notices ever does.

entities._comment: A second, smaller notice surface (city/personal notices, distinct from the Guild's own bounty board) -- ORIGINAL flavor copy, canon-safe (no invented named characters), voice-linted. entities.toast: A second board, smaller and less official: lost gear, room-for-rent scraps, one challenge to a duel that's clearly gone unanswered a long time.
entities.observe: Handbills and scraps overlapping the request board's edge. The Guild's actual business spills past its own furniture. Somebody wants a lost warhammer back. Somebody else is renting a room, quiet tenants only.

entities._comment: Renn Coldscale, Bronze-rank Drake, half of a bickering duo at the board -- profile in docs/design/character-profiles-staging.md. Reuses the `pc_drake_m` character-creation rig (ash-grey tint) rather than new art. talk_pool + a static dialogue fallback (no conversation graph -- inert-adjacent by design).
talk_pool: Four silver for a nest clear? Four? My arrows cost more than that if it goes badly.
Every posting on that board is an insult with a wax seal. I'm taking it anyway. Don't look smug.

dialogue.speaker: Renn
dialogue.text: Still four silver. Still an insult.

entities._comment: Ilvo Brackenhide, Bronze-rank Drake, the reasonable half of the duo. Reuses `pc_drake_f` (moss-green tint).

The pay's fair for Bronze work. Renn just likes the sound of his own complaining.

dialogue.speaker: Ilvo
dialogue.text: He'll take it. Watch.

entities._comment: Yelra, Bronze-rank Gnoll archer, waiting at a side table. Reuses `pc_gnoll_f` (tan-brown tint).
talk_pool: Bronze-rank, six months in. Long enough to know which jobs pay in coin and which pay in regret.
Quiet week. Short on the draws, long on daylight. I'll take quiet.

dialogue.speaker: Yelra
dialogue.text: Board's behind you, same as it was a minute ago.

entities._comment: Duty Sergeant Dresk Ashgrave -- the relocated watch_guard (see map comment above). talk_pool only (no conversation graph), inert-adjacent, matching Yelra/Renn/Ilvo's own precedent -- duty-mundane background presence, not a quest-giver v1.

talk_pool: Sergeant Ashgrave. If you're here to report something, the slate's on the wall. Write it plain.

Barracks business, filed here. Yours is filed at the gate.

dialogue.speaker: Dresk

entities.observe: Tidier than her schedule allows. A stack of gate-shift reports pinned under a paperweight shaped vaguely like a threat. She is almost never behind it. The gate keeps her busier than her own office does.
entities.toast: Watch Captain's desk. Empty, same as every other time you've walked past it.

entities.locked_toast: Barred, and empty behind the bars. You can tell by the quiet. Whatever ends up in here hasn't happened yet.
entities.observe: A single holding cell, iron-barred, straw swept into one corner. Duty-mundane, like everything else in this building — until it isn't.

entities.item_hint_toast: Nothing to shoot with. A bow in hand would do it.
entities.toast: You put an arrow in the straw. Not bad, for someone who still flinches at the draw.
